# Results — Study 205 (Three-Fund) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Three-fund portfolio
(60% VTI / 30% VXUS / 10% BND, annual rebalance, 5 bps one-way cost) measured against
100% US equity (SPY) and 60/40 (SPY+BND) on daily adjusted-close data from Yahoo Finance.
As-of **2026-06-15**. Common start: **2011-02-01** (VXUS launch month); end: 2026-06-15;
**n = 3,865 trading days (≈ 15.3 years)**. Content fingerprint: `2eaa8336f1fa`.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Role | Window | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| VTI  | US total market (three-fund leg) | 2011-02-01 → 2026-06-15 | Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF |
| VXUS | Intl ex-US (three-fund leg) | 2011-02-01 → 2026-06-15 | Vanguard Total Intl Stock ETF |
| BND  | US total bond (three-fund leg) | 2011-02-01 → 2026-06-15 | Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF |
| SPY  | US-only baseline | 2011-02-01 → 2026-06-15 | SPDR S&P 500 ETF |

## Main result — portfolio comparison (5 bps one-way, annual rebalance)

| Strategy | CAGR | Ann. Vol | Sharpe | Max Drawdown | Calmar | HAC *t* (annual) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Three-fund (60/30/10)** | **10.61%** | 15.27% | **0.737** | **−31.21%** | 0.340 | +5.17 |
| 60/40 (SPY+BND) | 9.56% | 10.41% | **0.929** | −21.03% | 0.455 | +6.12 |
| 100% US (SPY) | **14.11%** | 17.11% | 0.857 | −33.72% | 0.418 | +6.47 |

**Over the 2011–2026 sample**, the three-fund portfolio had the *lowest* risk-adjusted return
(Sharpe **0.737**) of the three competitors, lower than both the simple 60/40 (0.929) and
100% US equity (0.857). Its higher volatility relative to 60/40 without a matching return
premium is the core finding.

## Pairwise return difference test (three-fund − baseline, HAC t on annual diffs)

Bonferroni threshold for 3 simultaneous tests at 5%: **|t| ≥ 2.394**.

| Comparison | Mean annual diff | HAC *t* | Verdict |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| Three-fund **vs 100% US** | **−3.48%/yr** | **−4.90** | Three-fund **significantly trails** (|t| > threshold) |
| Three-fund vs 60/40 | +1.31%/yr | +1.70 | **Not significant** (|t| < threshold) |

**Three-fund vs 100% US:** trails by 3.48%/yr with a Bonferroni-adjusted t of −4.90 —
the VXUS international sleeve was a systematic return drag on this sample.

**Three-fund vs 60/40:** +1.31%/yr but t = +1.70, below the Bonferroni threshold (2.394)
— not statistically distinguishable. Higher raw return but also higher volatility and deeper
drawdown.

## International attribution — did VXUS help or hurt?

The three-fund (60 VTI / 30 VXUS / 10 BND) vs the no-international alternative
(90 VTI / 10 BND — same equity/bond ratio):

| Comparison | Mean diff | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| VXUS sleeve contribution | **−2.01%/yr** | **−3.25** |

The VXUS international sleeve subtracted approximately **2%/yr** relative to simply
allocating that equity weight to VTI. This is the central result of the international
home-bias debate on this sample: non-US equity underperformed US equity significantly
over 2011–2026. This is a sample-period outcome, not a structural truth — but it is the
honest verdict on the data.

## Bootstrap Sharpe confidence interval (three-fund)

| Estimate | 95% CI (CBB bootstrap) | Fraction of resamples < 0 |
|---|---|--:|
| 0.737 | [0.251, 1.247] | 0.1% |

The CI is wide (±0.5 Sharpe unit) due to the low-n annual-return regime. The three-fund
Sharpe is real (barely any resamples below zero), but the confidence intervals of all
three strategies overlap substantially — ranking is sample-dependent.

## Sub-period Sharpe breakdown

| Period | 3-fund Sharpe | US-only Sharpe | 60/40 Sharpe | 3-fund CAGR | US CAGR |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2011–2015 | 0.573 | 0.800 | 0.976 | 7.5% | 11.8% |
| 2016–2020 | 0.810 | 0.857 | 0.986 | 12.8% | 15.4% |
| 2021–2026 | 0.841 | 0.944 | 0.887 | 11.9% | 15.6% |

The three-fund trails the US-only baseline in every sub-period on Sharpe. The 60/40 wins
on Sharpe in all three sub-periods. No sub-period reversal: this is not a "mixed" result
that averages out — the three-fund genuinely underperformed on a risk-adjusted basis
throughout the entire sample, driven by international equity underperformance.

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** The three-fund portfolio is real and positive (Sharpe 0.74, t > 5),
  but it is *worse* than both baselines on a risk-adjusted basis over 2011–2026. The
  international sleeve was a statistically significant return drag (−2.01%/yr, t = −3.25).
  This is a sample-period result (2011–2026 was an exceptional decade for US stocks), but
  it is the honest verdict on the tape.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The three-fund is cheaply tradable (costs barely matter at
  annual rebalance), but "tradable" is not the same as "better than the alternatives."
  Relative to just buying SPY, it was a significantly worse return at similar volatility.
  Relative to 60/40, it offered more return but less Sharpe at higher drawdown — and the
  diff is not significant. A retail investor could implement it, but the case for
  complexity over SPY-only or 60/40 is not supported by this sample.
- **International contribution — HURTS.** The VXUS sleeve subtracted 2%/yr with t = −3.25,
  clearing the Bonferroni bar. This is the most structural finding: the "diversification
  benefit" of international did not materialise as a return premium over this sample.
